'''Nina Holden''' is a Norwegian mathematician interested in [[probability theory]] and [[stochastic process]]es, including [[graphon]]s, random planar maps, the [[Schramm–Loewner evolution]], and their applications to [[quantum gravity]]. She was a Junior Fellow at the Institute for Theoretical Studies at [[ETH Zurich]], and is currently an associate professor at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] of [[New York University]].{{r|cv|khrono}}

==Education==
As a student at [[Berg Upper Secondary School]] in [[Oslo]], Norway,{{r|berg}} Holden became the first woman to win the Abel competition, Norway's national Mathematical Olympiad.{{r|abel}} She competed in 2005 in the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]], where she earned an honorable mention with one of the two top scores on the Norwegian team.{{r|imo}}

She became a student at the [[University of Oslo]] in Norway, where she earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics and computational science in 2008 and a master's degree in applied mathematics in 2010. While a student in Oslo, she also visited the [[University of Oxford]] from 2006 to 2007.{{r|cv}}

After three years of work as an energy market analyst, she went to the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] for graduate study,{{r|cv|abel}} and completed her Ph.D. there in 2018.{{r|cv}} Her dissertation, ''Cardy embedding of random planar maps and a KPZ formula for mated trees'', was supervised by [[Scott Sheffield]].{{r|cv|mg}}

==Recognition==
In association with the 2021 [[Breakthrough Prize]]s, Holden was awarded one of three 2021 [[Maryam Mirzakhani New Frontiers Prize]]s, for early-career achievements by a woman mathematician.{{r|khrono|mmnf}} The citation reads: "for work in random geometry, particularly on Liouville Quantum Gravity as a scaling limit of random triangulations." The particular work refers to her joint work with [[Xin Sun]] on the convergence of uniform triangulations under a conformal embedding. The other two winners of the prize were [[Urmila Mahadev]] and [[Lisa Piccirillo]].{{r|mmnf}} She received the 2022 Viggo Brun Prize of the [[Norwegian Mathematical Society]], "for her exceptionally deep and broad contributions to probability theory, especially for her work on random surfaces and quantum gravity in two dimensions".{{r|brun}} In 2023, she was a recipient of the [[Rollo Davidson Prize]],{{r|rollo2023}} and in the following year, she was awarded the [[EMS Prize]] "for her profound contributions to probability theory and its applications to statistical physics, including results linking Liouville quantum gravity, the Schramm-Loewner evolution, and random triangulations".{{r|ems2024}}

Holden was elected to the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]] in 2026.{{r|dnva}}

== Personal life ==
Holden's mother, Marit Holden, is the Chief Research Scientist at the [[Norwegian Computing Center]].<ref name="l299">{{cite web | title=Nina Holden – 2021 Maryam Mirzakhani New Frontiers Prize | website=Breakthrough Prize | url=https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/3/L3888 }}</ref><ref name="d246">{{cite web | title=Marit Holden | website=NR | date=2021-03-16 | url=https://nr.no/en/employees/marit-holden/ }}</ref> Her father, Lars Holden, was its managing director from 2001 to 2022 and is the brother of [[Helge Holden]].<ref name="l299" /><ref name="y401">{{cite web | title=Lars Holden | website=NR | date=2021-03-16 | url=https://nr.no/en/employees/lars-holden/ }}</ref><ref name="i810">{{cite journal | last1=Holden | first1=Helge | last2=Holden | first2=Lars | title=Optimal rebalancing of portfolios with transaction costs | journal=Stochastics | volume=85 | issue=3 | date=2013 | issn=1744-2508 | doi=10.1080/17442508.2011.651219 | pages=371–394 | url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/17442508.2011.651219 | quote=The authors thank their brother Steinar Holden for valuable comments.| url-access=subscription }}</ref>
